title: Three Chefs and a Label-Reader Carry Food Into the First TIME100 Next India List
excerpt: Prateek Sadhu, Hussain Shahzad, New York's Chintan Pandya and creator Revant 'FoodPharmer' Himatsingka are the food names on TIME's inaugural 100-strong India list.
body:
• TIME's inaugural TIME100 Next India list, its first international extension of TIME100 Next, names 100 emerging leaders across business, entertainment, science, sports and advocacy.
  • Its food names span three chefs and a creator: Prateek Sadhu of Naar in Kasauli, Hussain Shahzad of Papa's in Mumbai, Chintan Pandya in New York, and Revant Himatsingka, the label-reading creator known as FoodPharmer.
  • The list was selected by TIME journalists in India and around the world; the issue is dated December 7, with a gala on December 12 at Mumbai's Jio World Convention Centre.

TIME has revealed the first TIME100 Next India list, recognising 100 emerging leaders whose work is shaping the country's future — and its food contingent captures how wide India's culinary influence now runs, from a Himalayan fine-dining kitchen to a New York dining room to a phone screen. The list, the first global expansion of TIME100 Next, was selected by TIME journalists in India and across the world, according to TIME's announcement.

Prateek Sadhu — the Himalayas on a fine-dining menu

Chef and restaurateur Prateek Sadhu, the force behind Naar in Kasauli, has built his reputation on Himalayan ingredients and regional flavours, taking local food traditions to a global fine-dining audience, NDTV Food reported. The recognition is a full-circle moment: Naar featured in TIME's World's Greatest Places list in 2025, putting the small hill-town restaurant on the global culinary map.

Hussain Shahzad — Indian fine dining, modernised

Mumbai chef Hussain Shahzad's restaurant Papa's is known for a 12-course tasting menu that combines Indian flavours with global culinary techniques, seasonal ingredients and storytelling. His place on the list rests on making Indian food feel contemporary without losing its roots.

Chintan Pandya — Indian food in New York

Chintan Pandya represents the diaspora side of the list. The New York-based chef has brought Indian flavours to an international audience through restaurants known for a modern, refined take on traditional dishes, blending the depth of Indian spices with contemporary technique.

Revant Himatsingka — the label reader

Better known online as FoodPharmer, Revant Himatsingka has built a large following by reading food labels on camera — explaining ingredients and hidden additives in the packaged food people eat every day. His inclusion puts a food creator and educator alongside the chefs, a sign of where influence over what India eats now sits.

The list around them

The four sit in a 100-name list that spans film, music, sport, business and science, with three worldwide covers: actor Alia Bhatt, Skyroot co-founder Pawan Kumar Chandana, and a group cover of filmmakers Aryan Khan, Payal Kapadia and Theja Rio. The TIME100 Next India issue is scheduled for December 7, and TIME will host the inaugural gala on December 12 at the Jio World Convention Centre in Mumbai.

"TIME100 Next India offers us a chance to acknowledge individuals defining what follows."

— Jessica Sibley, CEO of TIME

The food selections sit inside TIME's stated purpose for the list: to bring the stories of India's emerging talent to a global audience. That a Himalayan tasting-menu chef, a Mumbai fine-dining chef, a New York restaurateur and a label-reading creator all qualify underlines the point — influence over food in India no longer belongs to restaurant kitchens alone.

nri_angle: Chintan Pandya's New York kitchens put the diaspora inside India's culinary story, and FoodPharmer's label videos are staples of Indian family group chats worldwide.
